cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)

Experience with a variety of administrative operations activities such as events planning, basic fundraising processes, risk management planning, website design, accounting and payroll, and contracts and grants regulations and guidelines.

Knowledge of/involvement in the visual, written, and/or performing arts; career goals related to arts administration. Prior experience in event and/or program coordination. Prior experience with public relations or marketing.
Analytical and problem-solving skills and experience in short- and long-term strategic planning and customer service.
Experience in arts or humanities program administration.
Experience with grant writing, fundraising, donor stewardship, or sponsored-project development.
Experience with communications, public programming, or audience engagement.

The position manages the day-to-day programmatic and operational activities of the Arts Research Center (ARC), working closely with the Faculty Director to advance ARC’s intellectual and programmatic vision. The position plays a central role in planning and implementing ARC’s public programs, artist and scholar engagements, fellowships, workshops, student initiatives, communications, fundraising and grant activities, and other Center programs.

Under the programmatic direction of the Faculty Director, manages, plans, coordinates, and implements the full range of ARC programs and initiatives, including public programs, artist and scholar residencies and engagements, workshops, fellowship programs, seminars and salons, student-led initiatives, working groups, online programs, and new initiatives.

Develops program plans, timelines, partnerships, and implementation strategies; coordinates participants and campus and external partners; oversees event and program logistics; and represents ARC on and off campus.
Participates in short- and long-term program planning, assesses program effectiveness, and recommends improvements.
Works closely with the Faculty Director to translate ARC's intellectual and strategic priorities into successful programs.
Administrative and Operational Management - 25%
Manages ARC's day-to-day administrative operations, including purchasing, reimbursements, contracting, space and facilities coordination, and other routine administrative activities.
Monitors program and operating budgets and works with divisional staff on financial planning, forecasting, fiscal close, and other higher-level financial analysis and reporting.
Coordinates on human resources and other administrative processes as needed.
Participates in annual planning and resource allocation with the Faculty Director.
Performs other duties as assigned consistent with the scope and level of the position.
Grant and Gift Management - 10%
In collaboration with the Faculty Director and campus development partners, identifies and pursues grant and philanthropic funding opportunities.
Researches funding opportunities; coordinates and drafts proposals, narratives, budgets, and supporting materials; assists with grant stewardship and reporting; and tracks grant deliverables.
Supports the Faculty Director and development staff in donor cultivation, proposal development, and stewardship activities.
Communications and Public Engagements - 15%
Coordinates ARC communications and audience-engagement activities, including website content, newsletters, social media, program announcements, and other digital and print communications.

Develops and edits program descriptions, creates design assets and promotional materials and works with shared communications resources and campus partners as appropriate to increase visibility and engagement with ARC programs.
As needed, provides work direction to work-study students, graduate student assistants, interns, and temporary staff supporting ARC programs and events.
Provides orientation and training, assigns project-based work, coordinates schedules, and reviews work products.
Proficiency in administrative, budgetary, human resources, and financial principles and practices.
Ability to think creatively and independently on concepts requiring advanced analytical skills.
Advanced interpersonal skills including ability to work with diverse groups to achieve results.
Advanced oral and written communication skills.
Familiarity with and/or ability to quickly learn UC and campus policies, procedures, and systems.
Demonstrated program management skills, including the ability to manage a portfolio of projects and initiatives simultaneously.
